name: Woody House
detail: Considering that Hong Kong hotels generally have poor value for money, this place is actually quite good. I booked a single room at a lower price than usual, and fortunately, they upgraded me. The bed was big, but the space was cramped, so it would definitely not be suitable for two people. However, I recommend it for solo travelers. It doesn't have the service or cleanliness of an expensive hotel, but the bedding was clean, the staff were friendly, and you could drink water and coffee for free. The room had a large window, which provided good lighting. I stayed on the second floor and could see the building across the street, but I think it would be much better to stay on a higher floor. The location was excellent for me since I usually like the Wan Chai area. You do have to wait almost 5 minutes for hot water when showering, so keep that in mind. The bathroom floor gets wet while showering, so it would be more comfortable if a bathroom mat was provided.

name: Ramada Hong Kong Harbour View
detail: 1. The hotel prices in Hong Kong are generally quite high, but among them, there's a hotel that is really affordable and in a good location (2 minutes away from the subway station, with buses going to Central). 2. I was honestly worried because I heard it had a bad smell, but at first, I felt it was stuffy? However, once I turned on the ventilation, there was no smell at all. 3. I heard the bed was hard, but since I prefer hard mattresses, I slept very well. 4. They said the bathroom was narrow, but it turned out to be wider than expected since it was a room without a bathtub. 5. They said the room was small, but it was actually bigger than I expected!!! (Having experienced even smaller places in Japan, this size is excellent; I could put my luggage on the shelf in front of the window and use it.) 6. It was nice to have a refrigerator!! (You need to buy water.) 7. I arrived at one o’clock, but they quickly checked me in, which touched me. 8. The female staff were extremely kind! (They showed me around Hong Kong on a map.) 9. The blackout curtains blocked out the light, which allowed me to sleep very well. 10. They said the sound insulation was poor, and while it is noisy if people are talking loudly in the hallway, I prepared earplugs in advance and slept wonderfully (I usually wake up if it’s noisy since I’m sensitive). 11. I heard the hairdryer wasn't great, so I brought my own, and I was very satisfied. 12. When I turned on the air conditioning, it was cold, and when I turned it off, it would be hot, but during summer, we prepared a mini electric mat in advance, kept the air conditioning on to enhance room conditions, and slept really well with our backs warm. I was going to cancel in advance from Korea because the reviews were very bad after coming back from Macau and was considering switching hotels, but I think I was extremely satisfied since I prepared for the negative aspects ahead of time ❤️❤️❤️❤️ Things to prepare: 1. Earplugs (for when there's noise in the hallway) 2. Hairdryer (the hairdryer is somewhat mediocre) 3. Mini electric mat (it gets cold with the air conditioning, so keep it on for warmth) 4. It’s hot during summer, but we always pack thermal underwear for pajamas when we travel to Southeast Asia (with the air conditioning on).

name: Regal Airport Hotel
detail: Since my flight arrived at 04:20 in the morning, I chose this hotel which is directly connected to the airport. I thought it might be a waste to use the hotel so early in the morning, but after taking a shower, I was able to rest in bed for about three hours, making the rest of the day refreshing and enjoyable. Additionally, it was close to both the airport and the train station, so on my last day, I could drop off my luggage at the hotel and explore the city freely until it was time to check in for my flight, which was great.

name: B P International
detail: My stay at the Langham Place, Tsim Sha Tsui was extremely satisfying! During the check-in process, the front desk staff were friendly and highly efficient, and they surprised me with an upgrade to a top-floor room! The staff also thoughtfully informed me that the upgraded room required taking an elevator to the 24th floor and then walking up a small flight of stairs. Although climbing a few stairs was a minor downside, it did not affect my overall good mood at all. When I opened the door to the room, the most stunning feature was the breathtaking view. From the top floor, the sight is completely unobstructed, with excellent lighting; both the cityscape during the day and the sparkling nighttime view are incredibly refreshing. The room was clean and tidy, and the bed was comfortable, providing me a great night's sleep. The hotel is close to Kowloon Park, within walking distance to the MTR station and shopping malls, making it an excellent location. With friendly service and unbeatable views, the value for money is very high. The next time I come to Tsim Sha Tsui, this will definitely be my first choice again!

name: Mini Central
detail: The room was spacious, and the hot water was good, allowing for a comfortable stay. The staff's attitude was very friendly, and the facilities were clean, which was satisfactory. It is in a good location for shopping, but accessing it on foot is very difficult. I stayed for about two weeks, and there was a sudden disconnection of the Wi-Fi at one point. Overall, the satisfaction relative to the price was high.

name: Bishop Lei International House
detail: Came to Hong Kong for business meetings and stayed in a luxurious suite at the hotel. The room is fully equipped with a desk for work and an area for meetings. The hotel is located on Robinson Road in Mid-Levels, with a view of Central outside the window that offers a pleasant night scene. The front desk staff is very friendly, providing clear and complete information. The daily cleaning service is meticulous and thorough. I will choose this hotel again for my next business trip.

name: Regala Skycity Hotel by Regal Hotels
detail: Hong Kong Regal Airport Hotel Stay Review (Approximately 500 words) This time, I chose the Regal Airport Hotel in Hong Kong for my layover, and the overall experience far exceeded my expectations. It is absolutely the ceiling of cost-performance ratio around the airport! The hotel opened in 2022, featuring a modern and spacious design. The lobby, with marble accents and soft lighting, is open and tidy. The check-in process was smooth, and the front desk staff were gentle and patient. Communication throughout was unobstructed, and they kindly informed me of the free shuttle bus schedule. The geographical location is the biggest highlight, just a few minutes' drive from Hong Kong Airport. The hotel offers a free shuttle bus that runs regularly between the airport, Tung Chung MTR Station, and Disneyland. It's only a two to three-minute walk to the AsiaWorld-Expo, making it particularly convenient for attending concerts, catching early flights, or family outings, saving on expensive taxi costs. It's within walking distance to the 11 SKIES shopping mall, providing a one-stop solution for dining and shopping, maximizing travel convenience. The guest rooms are clean and bright, considerably more spacious compared to hotels in downtown Hong Kong at the same price point. The entire building features double-glazed soundproof windows, so even being close to the airport, there is no noise from planes taking off and landing, allowing for a very restful sleep. The bedding is soft and skin-friendly, and the toiletries are fully equipped. There are drinking water machines in the corridors, so you can bring your own cup to fill up, which is both environmentally friendly and convenient. The floor-to-ceiling windows offer a wide view; in some room types, you can watch the planes take off and land from the bed. The rooftop observation deck allows for enjoying sea views and sunsets in the evening, perfect for capturing the atmosphere in photos. The hotel has comprehensive facilities, with a 24-hour gym and an outdoor heated swimming pool, providing leisure options for families as well. The buffet breakfast is rich in variety, offering a complete range of both Western and Chinese food.

name: Ramada Grand Tsim Sha Tsui
detail: It's great to be able to stay alone in the city center of Hong Kong, where accommodation costs are always high, at this price. It wasn't inconvenient at all, but since the minibuses were running nearby, getting on and off was a bit challenging. The train station wasn't far, so I also used the train. The room size was about that of a Toyoko Inn single, very efficient without any waste, and the closet was a bit larger, which was convenient. Although small, there was a bathtub, and taking a shower was easy, but the floor got soaked to an embarrassing extent. There was an auto-check-in machine and a card drop box, so I spent my time without ever meeting the staff. The room was perfectly fine for just showering and sleeping. There were quite a few club-like places around where you could drink at night, which was fun. Don't forget your toothbrush and hairbrush.
area: Tsim Sha Tsui,Hong Kong - View on map

name: Burlington Hotel
detail: About a 5-minute walk from the Wanchai Station exit. It was easy to find since you just walk straight, and it wasn't far. They explained at the beginning that amenities and water are provided for a fee. The front desk staff was cheerful and kind. When I went to the hotel just to drop off my luggage, I was able to check into my room even though it was still in the 8 o'clock hour because they said it was ready. Lucky! The room had a large glass window that made it feel open, and it came with a refrigerator, a hairdryer, a TV, hand soap, shampoo, and conditioner. My room even had a microwave! The sheets, washbasin, and shower booth were clean and felt fresh. Since checkout was at 12:00, I was able to relax at my own pace, which was nice! There are various supermarkets, convenience stores, bakeries, and restaurants nearby, so I don’t think you would have any trouble. Additionally, popular places like Bakehouse, C dessert, Wanchai Market, and Amoy Street are all within walking distance, making it a great spot to explore. I think hotel prices in Hong Kong are generally high, and this place is also on the expensive side, which is the only downside, but the hotel itself was so good that I would definitely like to stay here again!

name: Best Western Hotel Causeway Bay
detail: I was impressed by the service of the staff. We stayed for 5 days and 4 nights. There was an issue with the faucet in the water tank, but the staff resolved it. The room was clean, and they changed the towels and bath towels every day. It was easy to find food; we could just walk out in the morning to look for restaurants. It's close to Times Square, and there is a dingding tram. Check-in and check-out were easy. I recommend staying here.
